content.title: How to watch the Warriors vs Knicks game without cable
content.text: Everything you need to know to watch the Warriors vs. Knicks game tonight.Billy CaddenThe Warriors head into the weekend still fighting to stay in the Western Conference playoff picture as they prepare to face the Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Golden State enters the weekend at 32-33 and continues to navigate life without Steph Curry, who remains sidelined with a lingering right knee injury. While the team appears relatively safe in the Play-In picture for now, every win matters as they try to improve their seeding before the postseason push. Unfortunately for fans, Curry won’t get the chance to put on a show at the Mecca of Basketball this time around.The Knicks, meanwhile, have been one of the best teams in the league this season and enter the weekend with a strong 42-25 record. New York has played consistently on both ends of the floor all year, and with Curry still out and Jimmy Butler already lost for the season, oddsmakers have the Knicks favored by 7.5 points. Even so, the Warriors have shown they can still compete without their stars, and a win at Madison Square Garden would go a long way toward keeping momentum alive in the tight Western Conference race.The Warriors vs Knicks game tips off Sunday night at 5:00 p.m. PST, and fans across the country can tune in with Sling TV and Peacock.When is Warriors vs Knicks? What: Golden State Warriors @ New York Knicks When: March 15, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. PST Where: Madison Square Garden, New York, NY TV: NBC and Peacock How to stream the Warriors vs Knicks game without cableOriginally slated to be a national showcase of Steph Curry live from Madison Square Garden, Sunday’s game will air across the country on NBC and Peacock, making it really easy to tune in even if you don’t have cable. While you could easily just snag an antenna from Amazon and flip to your local NBC station, we suggest signing up for a streaming service with live TV to catch as many games as possible. And our top pick for Warriors coverage is Sling TV.With Sling Select starting at just $29.99 here in San Francisco and carrying NBC, it’s one of the cheapest streaming subscriptions you’ll find. From there, you can upgrade to Sling Blue for $54.99/month for NBC and a heck of a lot more channels, or you can go all the way to Sling Orange & Blue for $69.99/month, though your first month is currently half-off. Here are all the ways to tune into the Warriors vs Knicks game with Sling (and the associated pricing here in the Bay: Sling TV 3-Month Prepay (Starting at $49.99 - $159.99 then monthly recurring payments) Sling TV Select (Starting at $29.99/month) Sling TV Blue (Starting at $54.99/month) Sling TV Orange & Blue (Starting at $69.99/month; half off your first month) If Sling doesn’t carry NBC in your area or you don’t want to use the platform for any reason, you can sign up for any of the other four major streaming services to catch all the action from the Garden: fuboTV ($48.99 for the first month, then $73.99/month with a 7-day free trial) DIRECTV STREAM ($89.99/month; there are no free trials right now for the base plan) Hulu + Live TV ($89.99/month with a 3-day free trial; also includes Disney+ and ESPN+) YouTube TV ($59.99/month for the first two months, then $82.99/month with a variable free trial)
